BigQueryOnQueryResultsConfig.description:
Poll-based trigger: run a SQL query on a schedule and emit NEW rows.

BigQuery has no native webhooks, so this acts as a scheduled query: on each
tick the user's SQL runs and only rows whose ``cursor_column`` is greater
than the last-seen cursor are emitted. The cursor high-water-mark lives in
durable node state (not config, which isn't persisted across polls) so
already-seen rows are never re-emitted, and the first poll baselines.

query.description: The SQL query to run on each poll (GoogleSQL). Must include the cursor column and be ordered so new rows have a higher cursor value.
query.title: SQL Query

cursor_column.description: Name of the timestamp/id column used to detect new rows. Only rows whose value in this column is greater than the last-seen value are emitted.
cursor_column.title: Cursor Column

use_legacy_sql.description: Use BigQuery legacy SQL dialect instead of GoogleSQL
use_legacy_sql.title: Use Legacy SQL

max_results.description: Maximum number of rows to scan per poll
max_results.title: Max Rows Per Poll

schedule.description: How often to run the query and check for new rows
schedule.title: Check Frequency

BigQueryOnQueryResultsConfig.title: BigQueryOnQueryResultsConfig

Service-account JSON key for server-to-server BigQuery access.

The primary auth method for automated/backend BigQuery access — a signed
JWT is exchanged for an OAuth access token per run. The project is read
from the key, so ``project_id`` fields can be left blank to default to it.
